episode_title: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

real_qa.q: How did Saadaa grow from December 2020 launch to profitability and what were the early revenue milestones
real_qa.r: Saadaa started in December 2020 with monthly revenue of 2 lakh rupees, quadrupled revenue in the next month, and tripled the business again after the first quarter of operations. By the fifth month of operations, they were doing about 40 lakhs in monthly business, achieved profitability by the sixth month, and maintained a ROAS above 10. They were selling only two core products initially: a basic essential bottom and plain bedding.
real_qa.requete: Saadaa revenue growth first year D2C

real_qa.q: Why did cotton yarn price increase impact Saadaa's home furnishing business and how did the company respond
real_qa.r: In 2021, during the COVID second wave, cotton yarn prices shot up by 2.5x, putting significant pressure on the home furnishing business. Rather than increase prices to consumers which would violate their values, Saadaa decided not to pass on the cost increase. This revealed that the buying pattern and consumption in home furnishing was very different from apparel, with consumers unwilling to pay significantly more, prompting them to focus the business model on apparel instead.

real_qa.q: What is Mahesh Tekwani's framework for hiring and building a team at a D2C brand
real_qa.r: Mahesh focuses on hiring people with two primary traits: a strong learning habit and self-organization. Rather than prioritizing performance and skill set alone, he emphasizes attitude, value system, and behavior—particularly a doer mentality and sense of ownership. He uses a two-axis framework evaluating both performance/skill and attitude/behavior, intentionally weighting attitude and self-learning culture more heavily than traditional corporate performance metrics.
real_qa.requete: D2C hiring framework team building attitude

real_qa.q: How does Saadaa differentiate its D2C strategy through packaging and brand storytelling
real_qa.r: Saadaa does not use plastic packaging; instead, all products are sold in reusable cotton bags made from waste fabric, with stitching done by partner NGOs rather than at mass scale. Product tags are plantable seed paper that customers can grow into plants. These decisions directly impact margins—cotton bags cost over 40 rupees compared to 3 rupees for plastic—but reflect core brand values. The company translates this philosophy to employees through town halls sharing stories and actions, ensuring the vision aligns across products, team, and customer experience.
real_qa.requete: Saadaa sustainable packaging cotton bags seed paper

real_qa.q: What is the critical insight about economies of scale for D2C brands scaling from micro to large
real_qa.r: Economies of scale operate as a bell curve, not a linear function. When very small, costs are low and margins are strong like a Kirana store. During the transitional growth phase, costs increase significantly due to administration and team building. Eventually at very large scale, costs plateau and margins improve. From micro to large scale, D2C founders face sustained margin pressure and cost increments and must maintain patience with the team, as compounding results appear only after extended effort.
real_qa.requete: economies of scale bell curve D2C growth

real_qa.q: Why did Saadaa focus exclusively on a single product for extended periods and what was the payoff
real_qa.r: Saadaa sold cotton pants as a single product for a year from August 2020 to December 2022, during which time the company did not grow even 1%. All effort was focused on building the right team, infrastructure, and culture. However, once these foundations were in place, growth recently kicked in—the team tripled from 30 people in March to 100 people, and revenue more than tripled in four months, demonstrating the compounding impact of patience and infrastructure investment.
real_qa.requete: Saadaa single product strategy compounding growth

guest.bio_context: Mahesh Tekwani is the founder of Saadaa, a D2C brand launched in December 2020 focused on sustainable essentials including apparel and bedding. He previously co-founded Blue Beds, a hospitality venture in Jaipur, and has experience in the real estate industry. His company has grown from a 100 square foot garage operation to over 100 employees, achieving profitability within six months of launch with initial ROAS above 10.
